messages.subject: [R-pkg-team] Bug#1088612: src:r-bioc-genomicranges: fails to migrate to testing for too long: triggers autopkgtest failure in r-bioc-variantannotation
messages.subject_clean: [R-pkg-team] Bug#1088612: src:r-bioc-genomicranges: fails to migrate to testing for too long: triggers autopkgtest failure in r-bioc-variantannotation
messages.body_plain:
On Thu, 28 Nov 2024 15:29:15 +0100 Paul Gevers <elbrus at debian.org> wrote:
> Source: r-bioc-genomicranges
> Version: 1.56.1+dfsg-1
> Severity: serious
> Control: close -1 1.56.2+dfsg-1
> Tags: sid trixie
> User: release.debian.org at packages.debian.org
> Usertags: out-of-sync
> 
> Dear maintainer(s),
> 
> The Release Team considers packages that are out-of-sync between testing 
> and unstable for more than 30 days as having a Release Critical bug in 
> testing [1]. Your package src:r-bioc-genomicranges has been trying to 
> migrate for 31 days [2]. Hence, I am filing this bug.

This is triggering an autoremoval, which is causing trouble for the ongoing 
r-bioc transition. Pinging this bug in order to attempt the autoremoval to get 
delayed, so that (hopefully) the r-bioc transition can finish, including 
migration for r-bioc-genomicranges.

Cheers,
Emilio

messages.subject_clean: [R-pkg-team] Bug#1067249: r-cran-bayestestr: autopkgtest timeouts on i386
messages.body_plain:
Since version 0.13.2-1of r-cran-bayesestr, the autopkgtest rely on r-cran-glmmtmb , which is not available for 32-bit architectures.

Testing locally by softening the dependency on r-cran-gmmtmb to ignore i386, the tests time hang for me as well.

So I've added a skip for autopkgtests if any dependencies are unavailable.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Michael

On 26-01-2025 16:51, Debian Bug Tracking System wrote:
> Changes:
>   r-cran-bayestestr (0.15.1-3) unstable; urgency=medium
>   .
>     * Team upload.
>     * d/tests/control: skip for missing dependencies, like r-cran-glmmtmb
>       on 32-bit architectures. Closes: #1067249

This can't be a fix for the issue I reported.... except when I actually 
read the bug report. Might have been a tiny bit more verbose in the 
changelog. (The test wasn't failing to install its dependencies, it was 
hanging *after* dependencies were installed, but you now added a 
dependency that isn't available on i386.)

I regret I added the skip-not-installable restriction to autopkgtest 
because it more often hides problems than that it does what it's 
supposed to do. If something doesn't work on a particular architecture 
it's better to excluded that architecture in the Architecture field.

Paul
